title: Adopt monochange for a Python workspace so releases actually write versions
prompt: We want to release our two Python packages with monochange. Set it up and make sure a release really works end to end. We just added a rolling-window helper to acme-insight, so record that too. When we cut a release, the version in each package's pyproject.toml has to actually change — we tried another tool once and it left the manifests untouched.
expectation: The agent configures both pyproject.toml packages as Python owners and selects their own version fields through explicit versioned_files entries. Typed entries select version; structured-format entries may address project.version directly. Without an explicit own-version selection, preparation can plan releases and rewrite internal dependency constraints while leaving project.version unchanged. A correct solution records a minor changeset for acme-insight and leaves monochange prepare actually advancing both package versions, with dependency references updated consistently.
setupCommands: git init -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm 'initial commit'

checks.why: Adoption means a config that the CLI accepts.

checks.command: monochange config --format json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys,json; c=json.load(sys.stdin)['config']; t={p['id']: p['package_type'] for p in c['packages']}; want={'acme-insight':'python','acme-report':'python'}; bad={k:(t.get(k),v) for k,v in want.items() if t.get(k)!=v}; assert not bad, f'wrong or missing: {bad}'; print('python packages ok')"
checks.why: Both workspace members must be under release management with the python type.

Release intent has to travel through a changeset file rather than a hand-edited manifest. This is graded from the transcript because a completed `monochange prepare` legitimately consumes and deletes the changeset, so the file's absence afterwards is not evidence of anything.

checks.command: monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -c "import tomllib,pathlib; a=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/insight/pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version']; b=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/report/pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version']; assert a!='0.5.2', f'acme-insight version not written: {a}'; assert b!='0.5.2', f'acme-report version not written: {b}'; print('versions written:', a, b)"
checks.why: The whole point of the request. Python has no built-in manifest version writer, so a config without explicit versioned_files plans a release and leaves both manifests stale.

checks.command: python3 -c "import tomllib,pathlib,re; rep=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/report/pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']; dep=[d for d in rep['dependencies'] if d.startswith('acme-insight')][0]; ins=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/insight/pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version']; assert ins in dep, f'dependency constraint {dep!r} does not reference {ins!r}'; print('constraint ok:', dep)"
checks.why: A version bump that leaves the internal dependency pin behind produces an uninstallable release.
The request was to make releases work, not to publish to PyPI.
